# Wave step 6: code review, in-place repair, and re-review dispatch

Nothing below has been executed. All verdicts are placeholders. HEAD stays at `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111` throughout. The wave's tracker indices remain `in_progress`, and nothing is committed until step 7.

## 1. Pre-dispatch check (parent)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD          # expect 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain      # expect: M  src/parse.ts / A  tests/parse.test.ts
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat             # expect empty: no unstaged edits
```

## 2. Initial code review (one per wave, over the integrated diff)

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: <wave summary from implementer reports>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Wave <w> tasks <n..m> from <plan-file>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts
Ask: production-ready?`
})
```

The payload has no `acceptance` field and no commit range. Because `HEAD_SHA` is `WORKTREE`, the reviewer runs:

```bash
git diff --stat 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
git diff --binary 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
```

This reads both staged and unstaged changes in the checkout. The new `tests/parse.test.ts` is visible because it is staged.

## 3. Review 1 returns FIX_FIRST (1 Moderate, `Behaviour-change: yes`)

This is review 1, so it carries no `TRAJECTORY:` line. The action is to dispatch fix 1:
- There is a single Critical/Moderate finding, so there is no fan-out.
- One implementer task carries the whole report.

**Before dispatch, freeze the reviewed state in the index:**

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -- src/parse.ts tests/parse.test.ts
git -C /workspace/project diff --quiet || echo "unexpected unstaged changes - stop"
```

**Fix dispatch (in place, no worktree):**

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<implementer-prompt.md filled>
Task: fix review finding(s) for wave <w> (owning task: the one whose Files: include src/parse.ts)
<full task text + spec path + Spec: anchors>
## Code review report (verbatim)
<entire FIX_FIRST report>
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts
TEST_CONTRACT: <task's Tests: block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>
COMMIT OVERRIDE: In-place wave repair. Do NOT commit and do NOT stage (no git add/commit).
Leave all edits uncommitted and unstaged; wave step 7 owns the commit.
Return status DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | NEEDS_CONTEXT | BLOCKED.`
})
```

## 4. After the implementer returns DONE (parent)

**Confirm the commit override held:**

```bash
git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD          # still 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
git -C /workspace/project diff --cached --stat 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111   # still only the reviewed deliverables
```

**Make the new file visible, then capture only the fix delta.** Because the reviewed deliverables are staged, the index-to-worktree diff contains only the fix:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -N -- tests/error.test.ts
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary > "$REPORT_DIR/wave<w>-fix1.delta"   # → ## Fix delta
```

**Stage the fix's deliverables, then run the scoped gate:**

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -- src/parse.ts tests/error.test.ts
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.ts)
```

The scoped gate runs only the wave's union command. `tests/error.test.ts` is not in `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS`, so it is not run here; the full suite belongs to the verify phase.

## 5. Re-review: spec review first, because `Behaviour-change: yes`

Spec review runs against the current implementation worktree, which is post-integration. It does not use a snapshot.

This counts as a first review: no `## Previous review report` marker and no `TRAJECTORY:` line. Its ordinal continues the owning task's spec-review count. For example, if that task's spec loop ended at review 1, this is review 2.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<spec-reviewer-prompt.md filled>
<full text of the task owning src/parse.ts>
Patch diff under review (the fix delta):
<contents of $REPORT_DIR/wave<w>-fix1.delta>
Spec: <absolute spec path in /workspace/project> — anchors: <task's Spec: anchors>
Tests contract (not commands): <task's Tests: block verbatim> ; Test: paths <...>
Start from the diff hunks (file:line), read every touched file in full from /workspace/project,
read deleted files from 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111. Never run tests.`
})
```

**Boundary: stop here.** The spec-review verdict has not arrived.

## Pending: code re-review (do NOT dispatch yet)

This is dispatched only after the spec review above is clean. It would be code review 2:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<review-1 FIX_FIRST report verbatim>
<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md>
## Fix delta
<contents of $REPORT_DIR/wave<w>-fix1.delta>`
})
```

The reviewer uses the same source as the first review: `git diff [--stat|--binary] 1111… -- .`.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
Below are the next commands and payloads, **not execution results**. The scenario does not supply the task text, spec path/anchors, or full reviewer report; those must be inserted from the existing plan and actual report rather than invented.

## 1. Initial wave code review

Keep `HEAD` at `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. **Do not commit the wave yet.** Its deliverables are already staged.

Dispatch:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review the integrated code-touching wave for production readiness.
Spec reviews have accepted its tasks and the scoped test gate has passed.

DESCRIPTION:
Integrated parsing changes in src/parse.ts and new tests/parse.test.ts.

PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
[Insert the full consuming wave's task requirements and plan reference.]

BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test tests/parse.test.ts

Use the current checkout, including staged and unstaged changes, against
BASE_SHA. Do not review HEAD~1..HEAD: HEAD has not advanced.

Read code and run Git commands; do not edit files.
Only the listed scoped test command may be run for verification.

Check correctness, maintainability, architecture, test quality, and plan
deviations. Follow the code-reviewer report format, including Verdict:,
Parallel-safe:, and Behaviour-change: footer lines.
`
})
```

The reviewer’s Git commands must use the integrated worktree as the review source:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat \
  1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .

git -C /workspace/project diff --binary \
  1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
```

These include the staged new `tests/parse.test.ts`; a plain unstaged `git diff` would not represent the wave.

## 2. Repair after the assumed `FIX_FIRST`

There is one Moderate finding, so dispatch one in-place implementer—not a fix fan-out. Carry the **entire actual review report**, including any Minors.

First preserve the report and create an external location for the fix delta:

```bash
REPAIR_REPORT_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
# Save the complete actual reviewer report to:
# "$REPAIR_REPORT_DIR/initial-code-review.md"
# This is orchestration material, not a repository deliverable.
```

Dispatch the repair:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Repair the integrated parsing wave's code-review findings in place.

[Insert the full original consuming task text, Tests: block, Test: paths,
authoritative absolute spec path, and Spec: anchors.]

[Insert the complete initial code-review report verbatim.]

The report's verdict is FIX_FIRST and Behaviour-change is yes.
Verify the finding against the code and implement the required repair.
The repair edits src/parse.ts and adds tests/error.test.ts.

The accepted wave deliverables are already staged:
- src/parse.ts
- tests/parse.test.ts

IMPORTANT COMMIT/STAGING OVERRIDE:
Do not commit, reset, unstage the existing wave, or stage your repair.
Leave your modifications unstaged and tests/error.test.ts untracked.
The parent will capture the fix-only delta, stage the repair, and obtain
SR then CR acceptance before committing the wave.

Follow TDD, self-review, and run only:

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test tests/parse.test.ts

Do not add a separate verification command for tests/error.test.ts.

Return an explicit status:
DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED.
Report changed files, scoped test results, and concerns.
For this in-place repair, DONE does not require a commit.
`
})
```

## 3. Capture only the repair delta, then stage it

After an acceptable implementer status, make the new repair file visible to the **unstaged** diff:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -N -- tests/error.test.ts

git -C /workspace/project diff --binary \
  > "$REPAIR_REPORT_DIR/fix-delta.patch"

git -C /workspace/project add -- src/parse.ts tests/error.test.ts

(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.ts)
```

The `git diff --binary` command intentionally has **no base SHA**. The index already contains the original wave; this captures only the unstaged repair relative to that index, including the intent-to-add test file. Using `git diff WAVE_BASE_SHA` here would incorrectly include the entire wave.

No commit occurs now. The review source remains:

```text
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
cwd: /workspace/project
```

## 4. Behaviour-changing repair: dispatch SR first

Because `Behaviour-change: yes`, the next actual dispatch is a spec review of the **fix delta against the current integrated implementation worktree**. No snapshot or pre-integration checkout is used.

```js
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review this behaviour-changing repair against the consuming task's contract.

[Insert the full consuming task text.]
Authoritative absolute spec path:
[Insert the existing absolute spec path in /workspace/project.]

Spec anchors:
[Insert the consuming task's exact Spec: anchors.]

[Insert the task's Tests: block and Test: paths verbatim as contract only.]

Patch under review:
[Insert the complete contents of the captured fix-delta.patch.]

Review the fix in the current integrated /workspace/project checkout.
Start from the patch hunks and read each touched file in full.
Read the anchored spec ranges yourself. Do not run tests.

This is the first spec review of this behaviour-changing fix, not a
spec-review re-review. Do not include a Previous review report
(re-review trigger) section or a TRAJECTORY line.
`
})
```

**Stop here: no SR verdict has arrived.**

### CR source after SR acceptance—not dispatched yet

Only if SR accepts the fix may the CR re-review be dispatched. Its source must still be the **whole integrated wave**, with the same base and `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`, not merely the fix patch. Its payload must include:

- `cwd: "/workspace/project"`, `agent: "code-reviewer"`, `async: false`.
- `BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.
- `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE`.
- `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts`.
- The complete initial CR report verbatim under  
  `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)`.
- The complete captured patch contents under `## Fix delta`.
- The prescribed CR trajectory instructions for re-reviews.

The wave remains **uncommitted** until its required reviews accept it; no acceptance or commit is implied here.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved. After keeps BASE_SHA at the recorded wave base with HEAD_SHA WORKTREE for both the initial and the pending code re-review, and both reviewers are told to run git diff --stat/--binary <base> -- . against the checkout rather than a commit range. The repair flow is intact and slightly more explicit than Before: it freezes the reviewed deliverables in the index (with a guard against unexpected unstaged edits), dispatches the implementer with a no-stage/no-commit override, verifies HEAD and the cached diff afterward, uses git add -N on tests/error.test.ts before capturing git diff --binary into the fix delta, and only then stages src/parse.ts and tests/error.test.ts before re-review. Because Behaviour-change is yes, SR is dispatched first against the live /workspace/project tree (whole-file reads from the checkout, deleted files from the base SHA, no snapshot), and CR is explicitly held as pending. HEAD and tracker indices stay unchanged, the scoped command is passed to CR, and the full suite is deferred to verify rather than run. This case touches integrated post-integration review, which the Change says to keep unchanged, so the chain-wave/chain-stop items in Expected to move are not exercised here; the only wording drift worth noting is that After dropped the '+ SDD extra checks' line from the initial CR payload, which is not a graded fact but could be restored to keep the payload identical to Before.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: both the initial CR and the pending CR re-review carry BASE_SHA equal to the wave base with HEAD_SHA WORKTREE and git diff against the integrated checkout; the repair implementer is told not to commit, reset, unstage the wave, or stage its edits; tests/error.test.ts is intent-to-added before a base-less git diff --binary and the repair is staged only afterwards; the behaviour-changing fix goes to SR first on /workspace/project with whole-file reads; and HEAD, task completion, and the wave commit stay untouched with only the scoped command run. Nothing in this post-integration scenario exercises the Change's chained implementer-to-SR dispatch, outputSchema restriction, or Verdict:-line parsing, so the Expected-to-move items are not observable here and no fact regressed. Two wording notes: After collapses the CR re-review into a bullet list instead of a concrete payload, which is acceptable but weaker evidence than Before's full subagent call—consider restoring the explicit payload (it costs little and makes the trajectory instructions and scoped command visible verbatim); and the extra `(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.ts)` after staging is fine for gates-preserved since it is the scoped command, but say explicitly that it is the same scoped gate and not an added verification step, to avoid any reading that the parent is expanding verification. Keep the explicit 'Do not stage your repair' line and the base-less diff explanation—those are what hold fix-only-delta.
